summary: Lesotho's Ministry of Home Affairs says every foreign citizen who wishes to visit must first obtain a visa through the Lesotho e-visa system, except citizens of countries with visa-abolition agreements with Lesotho and of some Commonwealth countries; it does not publish the list. The UK, Italian, Canadian and Australian governments say their citizens can visit without a visa.

It says driving standards and road conditions are poor and that animals roaming on the roads are a hazard, especially at night.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says weather conditions can change rapidly in mountainous regions and that even in summer it can become cold unexpectedly; during the winter months (June to August) it says to expect extreme cold and heavy snowfall in the mountains, which could lead to road and mountain pass closures, and to carry a blanket, warm clothes and a flashlight in case of snowfall or vehicle breakdown in mountain areas.

Canada's travel advice says you must have a four-wheel-drive vehicle to enter and depart Lesotho through the Sani Pass on the eastern border, and may need one in rural mountain areas connected only by dirt roads.
The UK government says the Lesotho loti is pegged to the South African rand on a one-to-one basis and both currencies are accepted throughout Lesotho.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lesotho?
faq.answer: Lesotho's Ministry of Home Affairs says every foreign citizen who wishes to visit must first obtain a visa through the Lesotho e-visa system unless their country has a visa-abolition agreement with Lesotho or is one of the Commonwealth countries it exempts; it does not publish the list. The UK government says British visitors can visit for up to 90 days without a visa, and Italy's foreign ministry says no visa is needed for tourism up to 90 days; Canada says no tourist visa is required for stays up to 30 days, and Australia says tourists can enter for up to 30 days without a visa.

faq.question: Can I visit Lesotho on a day trip from South Africa?
faq.answer: The UK government says all visitors to Lesotho must travel through South Africa, whether by air or land, and must meet South Africa's entry requirements, and that Lesotho border control and South African border control both need to stamp your passport. Canada's travel advice says you must have a four-wheel-drive vehicle to enter and depart Lesotho through the Sani Pass.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Lesotho?
faq.answer: The UK government says you can extend your stay by completing a 90-day temporary permit extension form and taking it to the Visa Application Centre in the Manthabiseng Convention Centre, Maseru; your passport will need to be valid for the extension period, and if you overstay without permission the authorities may detain you and will charge you weekly fines.

faq.question: Can I still apply for a Lesotho visa online?
faq.answer: Lesotho's Ministry of Home Affairs says visas are obtained through the Lesotho e-visa system, but no official source we could read offers a working online visa application for Lesotho. The Government of Lesotho's service charter lists the documents required for an entry visa.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Lesotho?
faq.answer: WHO's country list says Lesotho has no yellow fever requirement at entry; Australia's Smartraveller says you'll need a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Lesotho if you are travelling from a country where yellow fever occurs, and Italy's foreign ministry says it is mandatory for travellers over 9 months of age coming from countries at risk or who have transited for more than 12 hours through an airport in one. South Africa, which the UK government says all visitors to Lesotho must travel through, requires proof of vaccination from travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission, and from those who have transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of such a country, according to WHO.
